lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • citizen — a person living permanently in a particular society or country
  • headquarters — main offices
  • traffic police — an official who controls traffic
  • walker — a person who walks, especially for exercise or enjoyment

Spellings

travelling, brochure, strange, traffic, citizen, enquired, inform, vehicles.

Plural Forms

Adding 's': car → cars, house → houses. Adding 'es': bus → buses, match → matches. Adding 'ies': story → stories, party → parties. We add -s to most singular nouns to make plural nouns. Some words require -es at the end to convert them to plural nouns. These words end in -s, -x, -ch and -sh. Some words that end in -o also require -es at the end to change them to plural nouns. Words that end in -y followed by a consonant are converted to plural nouns by replacing -y with -i and adding -es to the end.

Irregular Plurals

goose → geese, wolf → wolves, man → men, mouse → mice, ox → oxen, tooth → teeth. Irregular nouns do not follow any particular rule to change to plural nouns.

Plural Forms

child → children, book → books, calf → calves, foot → feet, city → cities.

Learning to Spell

The completed words are: citizen, inform, stranger, enquire, traffic.

Pointing Words

This is my favourite breakfast. That dress is beautiful. I like these vases. Those apples are very juicy. This, that, these and those are used with nouns to refer to people or things. We use 'this' and 'these' for people or things close to us. We use 'that' and 'those' for people or things away from us.

Pointing Words

This is my book. That is your bag. These are my shoes. Those are his books.

The Past Continuous Tense

Sahar and Sofia were playing. He was not writing a letter. We were getting late for the flight. They were running for a race. Was Salma going to Karachi? The past continuous tense is used to express an ongoing action in the past. Affirmative: Subject + was/were + base form of verb + -ing + object. Negative: Subject + was/were + not + base form of verb + -ing + object. Interrogative: Was/Were + subject + base form of verb + -ing + object?

The Past Continuous Tense

Affirmative: I was reading a book. They were playing cricket. Negative: I was not reading a book. They were not playing cricket. Interrogative: Was I reading a book? Were they playing cricket?

Connectors

Yesterday, I had a great time with my friends. Firstly, I met them in a park. Secondly, I bought a beautiful scarf for my sister and I went out to have dinner with my family. Finally, I returned home and completed my speech for the speech competition. Connectors are used to show the order in which things happen. 'Firstly', 'secondly' and 'then' are some connectors.

Connectors

Firstly, I wake up early in the morning. Secondly, I brush my teeth and take a bath. Then, I eat my breakfast and go to school. Finally, I return home and do my homework. This short paragraph uses connectors to show the sequence of a daily routine.

Hyphens

The hyphenated words are: well-known, thirty-two, mind-blowing, four-minute. He is a well-known writer. There are thirty-two students in my class. The show was mind-blowing. It was a four-minute walk to school. Hyphens are used to make compound numbers — The building has twenty-one floors; to join two words — Ahsan is a good-looking boy; and between the numbers in a fraction — He ate one-fourth of the bread.

Letter Writing

Dear Ali,

How are you? I am writing to share some traffic and safety rules for pedestrians. Always walk on the footpath. Cross only at zebra crossing. Look to your left and right before crossing the road. Never run on the road. Obey traffic signals and the traffic police.

Take care.

Your friend, Ahmed.

Letter conventions are: address, date, salutation, body, closing.

Expository Paragraph

My grandfather has given me a computer as a present. I am about to set up my new computer. There are so many different parts! I do not know where to start. The instructions manual can help me. It tells what each part is and how to attach it. I will follow the instructions step by step. First, I will connect the monitor and the (CPU). Next, I will connect the keyboard, mouse and speakers. Then, I will turn on the computer.

Expository Paragraph

First, I take a bag and check that it is clean. Next, I put my clothes in the bag. Then, I add my toothbrush, soap and towel. Finally, I put my books, water bottle and snacks in the bag, and I am ready for the trip. This is a short expository paragraph on how to pack a bag for a trip.

Creative Writing

Traffic rules can be followed in daily life in these ways: always walk on the footpath, cross at zebra crossing, look left and right, fasten the seatbelt in a car, and obey traffic signals.

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Rainy Day

Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots (long boots) are used to get shelter from rainwater. In the rain, a raincoat and gumboots can be worn and an umbrella can be taken. On a rainy day, hot pakoras and soup are good to eat. While it rains, indoor games like ludo can be played.

The Poem

Little drops of water,
Little grains of sand,
Make the mighty ocean
And the pleasant land.

So the little moments,
Humble though they may be,
Make the mighty ages
Of eternity.

So the little errors
Lead the soul away,
From the paths of virtue
Into sin to stray.

Little deeds of kindness,
Little words of love,
Make our earth an Eden,
Like the heaven above.

The poem 'Little Things' is by Julia A. Carney.

About the Poem

The poem is about how small things are important and make big things. Little things make a person happy because a kind word, a smile or a small gift can bring great joy.

The Meaning of Little

'Little' means small in size or amount. In this poem it also means humble and simple — but not useless, because little things together make mighty things.

The Last Stanza

The last stanza means that little deeds of kindness and little words of love make our earth like Eden (paradise), just like the heaven above. Small acts of kindness make the world a beautiful place.

An Act of Kindness

Once an old man was helped to cross the road and his bag was carried for him. He smiled and thanked the helper. He prayed for the helper. The helper felt very happy that day.

Rhyming Words

Pairs of rhyming words in the poem are: sand — land, away — stray, love — above. There is also the near-rhyme be — eternity.

An Act of Kindness

Once a lunch was shared with a classmate who had forgotten his lunch box. He was very happy and thanked the one who shared it.

Message of the Poem

The message is that little things are important and not useless. We should not look down upon them. Everything has its importance, no matter how little it may be. Little deeds of kindness and words of love make the world a heaven.

Map Directions

The direction of the post office from the school is West. The direction of the hospital from the playground is South-East. The direction of the playground from the hospital is North-West. The direction of the police station from the post office is South-East. On the map grid, the school is in the middle, the post office is to its west, the hospital is to its east, the playground is to the north, and the police station is to the south. The Direction Key is: North up, South down, West left, East right.

Key Facts

  • The poem 'Little Things' is written by Julia A. Carney.
  • The poem highlights the importance of little things.
  • Little grains of sand make the pleasant land.
  • An ocean is made up of little drops of water.

Analytical Reading

Activity: Use the internet and read about different rivers in Pakistan. Collect some interesting facts about them and share them with your classmates.

Stress, Rhythm and Intonation

Now another day is breaking. Sleep was sweet and so is waking. Dear Lord, I promised You last night never again to sulk or fight. Stress is the force used to pronounce words or syllables. Rhythm is the repeated pattern of sounds and movements. Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice while speaking. The word in the stanza is read as 'sulk', which fits the sense of the line — promising never again to sulk or fight.

Non-verbal Communication

The given signs say: celebration, angry, consoling. Non-verbal communication is when we use different body parts and gestures to communicate our feelings and emotions. Tone is the way we speak. Tone and non-verbal communication are different ways to convey messages.

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • eternity — infinite or unending time
  • pleasant — enjoyable
  • mighty — very large and powerful
  • stray — to lose direction
  • virtue — a good act

Regular Verb Forms

allow → allowed → allowed. behave → behaved → behaved. jump → jumped → jumped. talk → talked → talked. Past and past participles of regular verbs are formed by adding '-d' and '-ed'.

Regular Verb Forms

enjoy → enjoyed → enjoyed. kick → kicked → kicked. need → needed → needed. punish → punished → punished.

Learning to Spell

The correct spellings are: mighty, heaven, eternity, virtue, pleasant.

Question Words

The correct question words in order are: Where for the new school, Which for the storybook, What for the favourite game, Why for looking so happy, and Who for the person absent today. Question words are used to ask questions.

Question Words

When is used to ask about time or any occasion. Example: When will you go to Dubai? How many is used to ask about the number of countable nouns. Example: How many people work in his company? How much is used to ask about quantity and the price of uncountable nouns. Example: How much sugar would you like in your tea?

Question Words

Examples with When: When will you come to my house? When is your birthday? Examples with How many: How many books do you have? How many brothers do you have? Examples with How much: How much water do you drink daily? How much money do you have?

The Simple Future Tense

They will buy a new car at the end of this month. She will not go to school tomorrow. It will rain tomorrow. Will he plan starting a new business? I will play football with my friends. The student will not appear in the exams this year. The simple future tense refers to actions and events that will happen in future. Affirmative: Subject + will/shall + base form of verb + object. Negative: Subject + will/shall + not + base form of verb + object. Interrogative: Will/shall + subject + base form of verb + object?

The Simple Future Tense

I will visit my grandmother tomorrow. We will play cricket on Sunday. She will read a new book tonight. They will go to Murree in summer. He will buy a new bicycle next month.

Kinds of Sentences

Instructions: Fry the onion for 5-7 minutes. Take your medicine before sleeping. Read the given non-verbal cues. Commands: Clean your room. Sit down. Exclamatory Sentences: What a lovely waterfall! Wow, you won a gold medal! What a cold day! Command sentences are used to give commands. We use a full stop at the end of these sentences. These sentences are also called imperative sentences. Instructional sentences give instructions on how to do things. These sentences end in a full stop. Exclamatory sentences show sudden feelings and emotions. They end with an exclamation mark.

Kinds of Sentences

Do your chores after breakfast — Command. Serve drinks with the meal — Instruction. Wow, what a lovely dress! — Exclamatory.

Questions with Do and Does

Do you play hide and seek? — Yes, I play hide and seek. Do they live in Karachi? — No, they do not. Does she like Italian food? — Yes, she likes it very much. Does he work in a bank? — Yes, he does. Do and does are also used at the start of a sentence to ask a question. Such questions end with a question mark (?).

Questions with Do and Does

Do you like mangoes? Do they play hockey? Does she sing well? Does he go to school by bus?

Central Idea of the Poem

The poem 'Little Things' highlights the importance of little things. It teaches us that little things are not useless. Therefore, we should not look down upon them. Everything has its importance, no matter how little it may be.

Central Idea of the Third Stanza

The third stanza teaches us that little errors can lead the soul away from the paths of virtue into sin to stray — small mistakes, if repeated, can take a person away from goodness into wrongdoing.

Creative Writing: Rhyming Poem

Rhyming pairs: ball — tall, play — day, toys — joys, books — looks.

My favourite thing is my little ball,
I bounce it high against the wall.
I play with it all through the day,
And with my toys I laugh and play.

An Act of Kindness

Once I helped an old man cross the road. He smiled and thanked me warmly. I felt very happy from inside. He prayed for my success. From that day, I always try to help people in need.

Questions with Do and Does

  • Do you like mangoes?
  • Does Ali go to school?
  • Do we have class today?
  • Does she speak English?

mcqs.q: What does the word 'eternity' mean?
mcqs.why: 'Eternity' means infinite or unending time; 'virtue' means a good act and 'mighty' means very large and powerful.

mcqs.q: What is the past form of 'allow'?
mcqs.why: Past and past participles of regular verbs are formed by adding -d or -ed: allow → allowed → allowed.

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about time or an occasion?
mcqs.why: 'When' is used to ask about time or any occasion: 'When will you go to Dubai?'

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about the number of countable nouns?
mcqs.why: 'How many' asks about the number of countable nouns: 'How many people work in his company?'

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about quantity or price of uncountable nouns?
mcqs.why: 'How much' asks about quantity and the price of uncountable nouns: 'How much sugar would you like in your tea?'

mcqs.q: Which sentence is in the simple future tense?
options: She will not go to school tomorrow.
mcqs.why: 'Will not go' refers to an action that will happen in the future: Subject + will/shall + base form of verb.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is a command?
options: Fry the onion for 5-7 minutes is an instruction only
Wow, you won a gold medal!
mcqs.why: Command sentences give commands and end with a full stop: 'Clean your room.' 'Sit down.' — they are also called imperative sentences.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is exclamatory?
mcqs.why: Exclamatory sentences show sudden feelings and emotions and end with an exclamation mark: 'What a cold day!'

mcqs.q: Which question word fits: '___ for the person absent today'?
mcqs.why: The lesson's order is: Where for the new school, Which for the storybook, What for the favourite game, Why for looking so happy, and Who for the person absent today.

mcqs.q: What is the central idea of the poem 'Little Things'?
options: Little things are important; everything has its importance, no matter how little it may be
mcqs.why: The central idea is that the poem highlights the importance of little things; we should not look down upon them because everything has its importance.

lessons.title: Reading and Sounds Review
lessons.notes_html:
Intonation

Do you brush daily? — rising intonation, because it is a yes-no question. Where is your school? — falling intonation, because it is a wh-question. We should obey our parents. — falling intonation, because it is a statement. Hurrah! We have won the match. — falling intonation, because it is an exclamation.

Non-verbal Communication

The given signs say: celebration, angry, consoling. Non-verbal communication means using body parts and gestures to communicate feelings and emotions.

Talking to Strangers

If a stranger tries to be friendly, a student should not talk to him or accept anything from him. The student should step away, say 'No!', leave quickly and tell his or her parents or teacher. Nothing should ever be taken from a stranger, and everything should be shared with parents.

The Fox and the Stork

The fox invited the stork to his house to play a trick on him and make fun of him.

Traffic Rules

Three traffic rules are: Fasten your seatbelt. Cross only at zebra crossing. Always walk and never run. Other traffic rules are: follow traffic signals, obey traffic police, and look to your left and right before crossing the road.

Respect for Others

We should respect others because Allah (SWT) has made us all equal. Everyone has value, and we should never ridicule or degrade anyone for any reason.

Parts of Speech

  • Noun — fox, stork
  • Verb — invited, served
  • Pronoun — he, him
  • Adjective — clever, tasty
  • Adverb — happily, calmly
  • Preposition — in, to
  • Conjunction — and, but

mcqs.q: Which sentence has rising intonation, and why?
options: 'Do you brush daily?' — it is a yes-no question
mcqs.why: Yes-no questions have rising intonation: 'Do you brush daily?' rises; wh-questions, statements and exclamations fall.

mcqs.q: What is non-verbal communication?
options: Using body parts and gestures to communicate feelings and emotions
mcqs.why: The review defines non-verbal communication as using body parts and gestures to communicate feelings and emotions.

mcqs.q: What should a student do if a stranger tries to be friendly?
options: Not talk to him or accept anything; step away, say 'No!', leave quickly and tell parents or teacher
mcqs.why: The review repeats the safety rule: never take anything from a stranger, step away, say 'No!', leave quickly and share everything with parents.

mcqs.q: Why did the fox invite the stork to his house?
options: To play a trick on him and make fun of him
mcqs.why: The review says the fox invited the stork to his house to play a trick on him and make fun of him.

mcqs.q: Which three traffic rules are listed in the review?
options: Fasten your seatbelt; cross only at zebra crossing; always walk and never run
Use a phone, run across, ignore signals
Sit in front, stand in the car, cross anywhere
mcqs.why: Three traffic rules are: fasten your seatbelt, cross only at zebra crossing, and always walk and never run; also follow signals and obey traffic police.

mcqs.q: Why should we respect others?
options: Because Allah (SWT) has made us all equal and everyone has value
mcqs.why: We should respect others because Allah (SWT) has made us all equal; everyone has value and we should never ridicule or degrade anyone.

mcqs.q: Which word is a verb in the review's parts of speech?
mcqs.why: Verb — invited, served; Noun — fox, stork; Pronoun — he, him; Adjective — clever, tasty.

mcqs.q: Which word is an adverb in the review's parts of speech?
mcqs.why: Adverb — happily, calmly; 'in' and 'to' are prepositions and 'and/but' are conjunctions in the list.

mcqs.q: What do the given non-verbal signs say?
mcqs.why: The given signs say: celebration, angry, consoling — feelings communicated without words.

mcqs.q: Which word is a conjunction in the review's list?
mcqs.why: Conjunction — and, but; they join words and sentences, while 'in' is a preposition and 'he' is a pronoun.

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing Review
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • harsh — severe, rough, unkind
  • degrade — to make people feel that they have no value
  • jogger — a person who runs slowly for exercise
  • stranger — a person that you do not know
  • mighty — very large and powerful

Tenses

The fox is degrading the stork — Present Continuous Tense. Did the children sleep late? — Simple Past Tense (interrogative). Ahsan takes out the brochure — Simple Present Tense. They will visit your house soon — Simple Future Tense. Ali was talking with his friend — Past Continuous Tense.

Hyphens

This building has thirty-four floors. He has eaten one-fourth of this cake. He is a well-known artist.

Kinds of Sentences

Instruction: Fry the onion for 5-7 minutes. Command: Clean your room. Exclamatory sentence: What a lovely waterfall!

Connectors

Sunday was a great day. I spent that day with my friends. Firstly, we visited the National Museum with our father. Secondly, we went to the nearby park and played cricket. Finally, we ate pizza and fries in the evening.

Story Writing: A Brave Girl

  • Character — a brave girl
  • Setting — her street
  • Plot — she sees a small boy in danger from a stray dog
  • Conflict — she is afraid but decides to act
  • Resolution — she saves the boy and everyone praises her bravery

Activity: Make a mind map about the topic 'A brave girl' and write a story with the help of the mind map.

The book content ends with Review-4. The last page of the book is the national anthem, which has no exercises.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'degrade' mean?
options: To make people feel that they have no value
A person you do not know
mcqs.why: 'Degrade' means to make people feel that they have no value; 'harsh' means severe, rough, unkind and 'jogger' is a person who runs slowly for exercise.

mcqs.q: What does 'harsh' mean?
mcqs.why: In the review vocabulary, 'harsh' means severe, rough, unkind; 'mighty' means very large and powerful.

mcqs.q: Which tense is 'The fox is degrading the stork'?
mcqs.why: 'Is degrading' shows an action going on now, so it is the Present Continuous Tense.

mcqs.q: Which tense is 'Ahsan takes out the brochure'?
mcqs.why: 'Takes out' is the base action in the present, so it is the Simple Present Tense.

mcqs.q: Which tense is 'They will visit your house soon'?
mcqs.why: 'Will visit' shows a future action, so it is the Simple Future Tense.

mcqs.q: Which tense is 'Ali was talking with his friend'?
mcqs.why: 'Was talking' shows an ongoing action in the past, so it is the Past Continuous Tense.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses a hyphen correctly?
options: This building has thirty four floors.
He is a well known artist.
He has eaten one fourth of this cake.
mcqs.why: Compound numbers take a hyphen: 'thirty-four floors' and 'one-fourth of this cake'; 'well-known artist' also needs one.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is an instruction?
mcqs.why: 'Fry the onion for 5-7 minutes' gives an instruction on how to do something; 'Clean your room' is a command and the others are exclamations.

mcqs.q: Which connector begins the museum-visit paragraph's second step?
options: Firstly, we visited the National Museum
Secondly, we went to the nearby park and played cricket
Finally, we ate pizza and fries
mcqs.why: The connectors paragraph runs: Firstly — National Museum; Secondly — the park and cricket; Finally — pizza and fries in the evening.

mcqs.q: In the story 'A Brave Girl', what is the conflict?
options: She is afraid but decides to act to save a small boy from a stray dog
mcqs.why: The story plan says: Conflict — she is afraid but decides to act; Resolution — she saves the boy and everyone praises her bravery.
